generated_from: ACS PUMS 1-year (Census microdata API), BLS ECI, BEA NIPA (via FRED), Census ASPEP govsemp, CBO 2024.
deflator: Real wages in constant 2026 dollars: each year's wage deflated by CPI-U to the latest available month (FRED CPIAUCSL). CPI-U-RS is the documented choice for any pre-2005 splice; over 2005-2023 CPI-U and CPI-U-RS are methodologically converged.

flag_caveats.small_cell: Fewer than 100 unweighted PUMS respondents in this cell — treat as indicative; standard error is wide.
flag_caveats.wages_only: Wages/salary only — excludes the benefits and pension value where public compensation is relatively richer.
flag_caveats.top_coded: ACS PUMS top-codes very high wages, so the public-private gap at the top is a floor; the true private lead is likely larger.
flag_caveats.median_granularity: ACS reports wages in rounded amounts, so a median can sit on a common round-number salary. Medians are interpolated within the bracket (the standard linear method); even so, read small median differences as approximate and weight the top-of-field comparison, which is far more separated.

quantile_method: Weighted quantiles use linear interpolation (Hazen plotting position), the standard convention for survey weights.

citations.cbo_2024: CBO, Comparing the Compensation of Federal and Private-Sector Employees, 2022 (April 2024). https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59970
citations.biggs_richwine: Biggs & Richwine (AEI), composition-adjusted public pay premia.
